doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing in Gene Harris's Philip Morris band
summary: The band backed singers like B.B. King and Diane Reeves, took solos, and toured Russia, the Philippines and Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So it was an all star band.

Well, it was a big band. I mean it was just a band. I mean, you know. An all star band, and we – Gene Harris' band. And it was like uh, -- Well, it was like a band backing up the singers and also backing up whoever played. You know. So, you know, the piano player would play, and we'd back that up. And then maybe they'd play a blues and the saxophones would play. And Ray would play something, and the band would back that up.
So everybody in the band was essentially a soloist as well then?
Um.
No, not really?
Well, I mean, everybody in the band took a solo. We'll put it that way. But they, you know, like – I've got a tenor, alto, flute and soprano. Like I played tenor in the band.
Uh-huh (affirmative).

So, but I mean that's what it was. Because Gene told me at first, he said, "Joe, I want people and you bring all your instruments, because I'd like people to play them all." You know. We'd play them all.
Uh-huh (affirmative).
And I wound up playing tenor. I mean, that was it. You know. Se la vi. You know.
[laughter]
So essentially that was the case of a sponsor saying I'll underwrite this tour for this particular group. And how long a tour was it?
Oh, we did a couple, a few of them.
Ah.

We did – We went from – We went to Russia and went all over the Philippines. All over Europe. I don't think we did Asia. The closest we got was the Philippines. And it was pleasant seeing all the guys. You know, like Frank Weston and Jerry Dogin (phonetic sp.). You know, but then mostly like with the tour we played for B.B. King, and we played for a girl. I saw her yesterday. I showed you the picture. FEMALE: Diane Reeves?
Diane Reeves. Yeah. Diane Reeves. It was nice. You know, like, you know. Basically, that's what it was. Basically, it was a band playing for people. That's what it was. It wasn't like Sad and Mel.
All right. So you were playing behind –

It wasn't like Sad and Mel playing music. I mean, you know, like playing some things and then band playing. You know. When the band would play, we'd play like Old Man River or you know. I think Gary played Lover. You know.
Uh-huh (affirmative).
We played the blues, you know. (Indiscernible). You know.
